title: The calf of gold
hookLine: while Musa is on the mountain the people make a golden calf, and Harun tries to hold them
carry: wait for the one who's coming back
tomorrow: Eleven stars, the sun and the moon

lines: THE GOLD GOES INTO THE FIRE.
cards: The teacher leaves the room for five minutes. The manager takes a vacation, and by Thursday nobody's following the plan. The people have just walked through the sea on dry ground and seen Pharaoh's army drown.
Then Musa goes up the mountain to meet his Lord, and leaves his brother Harun in charge. He's gone forty nights.
And in that time, the people's gold ornaments go into the fire, and a man called the Samiri brings something out of it.

teach.b: Surah Ta-Ha. The Samiri brings out a calf, a body that makes a lowing sound, and the cry goes up: this is your god, and the god of Musa, but he forgot. Harun, in the Qur'an, doesn't go along with it.
He stands up: my people, you're only being tested by this. Your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.

teach.h: UNTIL MUSA COMES BACK TO US.
teach.b: Their answer gives the whole story away: we will not stop devoting ourselves to it until Musa comes back to us. They said they were waiting for Musa.
And while they waited, they made a calf, filling the empty time with something they could see and touch. Musa comes down angry and grieved.
He grabs his brother by the beard and head: what stopped you, when you saw them going astray?
Harun says: son of my mother, don't seize my beard or my head. I was afraid you'd say I had split the Children of Israel. He'd held on as best he could without tearing the people in two.

Then Musa turns to the Samiri, and the calf is burned and scattered into the sea. Who the Samiri was, the Qur'an doesn't say, and scholars have offered many answers. That ends our two weeks with Musa.
A chest on the river. Asiya's arms. His mother's cooled eye.
A blow and a flight. Faqir. Fire on the mountain.
The staff. A loosened tongue. A gentle word.

teach.h: WAIT FOR THE ONE COMING BACK.
teach.b: And a calf made by people who couldn't wait.

how: Muslims honor Harun as a prophet and brother of Musa, and the story of the calf is taught as a warning against worshipping anything made by hand; it is told in several surahs.

games.q: you're Harun, left in charge. the people are gathering around a golden calf that makes a lowing sound. what do you do?
o: join them to keep the peace.
warn them: you're only being tested. follow me.
leave and go find Musa on the mountain.
games.why: Harun warned them. they refused until Musa came back. later he told Musa he'd feared splitting the people apart.

practice: When you're waiting, for news, for an answer, for someone to come back, what do you fill the time with: the phone, food, work, shopping, or worrying, which can be its own golden calf?
Don't judge it; just find the thing you reach for when the waiting gets long, look at it honestly, and then sit in the waiting itself, empty-handed. If you pray, you can ask for patience in the gap.

wordCard.voice: 'Ijl, calf: what the Samiri made from the people's gold while they said they were waiting for Musa.
